content:

title: How to Use JEV by TypeSafe with Innflow
content:
Pending editorial brief. Research checked on 30 September 2026. Not published or scheduled. ## Editorial angle A practical, reproducible guide to the current Innflow AI Decision node using JEV. Use a support-request triage example throughout. Explain the account prerequisite first: the node must be enabled for the reader’s workspace. Do not promise that every account can find it or invent an OAuth connection screen for TypeSafe. ## Opening hook The useful first JEV workflow is one decision you can inspect. Start with a support message, define the allowed categories, and connect the result to a clear next step. Teach readers to check both the typed answer and the review branch before enabling consequential actions. ## Step-by-step article outline 1. Confirm AI Decision access in the workspace and choose a simple, reversible test workflow.
2. Add an intake step that supplies text, such as a form submission or an existing request record. Use only a supported trigger verified in the workspace.
3. Add AI Decision and configure Input using text from the previous step. Only selected input is sent for evaluation.
4. Add a named Choice question called category with billing, technical, and other criteria. Use clear descriptions of each category.
5. Add an optional Boolean urgency question or Score rubric for evidence completeness. Explain that Innflow labels the yes/no question Boolean while TypeSafe calls its primitive Noul.
6. Review policy thresholds and understand Decided versus Needs review.
7. Connect Decided to explicit category handling and Needs review to a person or additional information. The Decided handle does not itself select a category-specific action.
8. Run labeled examples, inspect the stored answers and execution result, and revise the input or rubric where needed.
9. Add production actions only after verifying permissions, error paths, and observed quality.
10. Frequently Asked Questions and a build-your-first-decision-workflow CTA. ## Configuration example for the draft Use a configuration example for AI Decision, not a claimed importable whole-workflow format. Input is an explicit previous-step text variable. Questions: category (Choice), urgent (Boolean), completeness (Score). Keep question IDs unique. The current Innflow contract supports 1–8 questions, map-based Choice criteria, and an ordered list for Score criteria. Default output variable is decision. ## Outputs and policy details to explain Show decision.status and decision.answers.category.choice, plus the category probabilities. Boolean answers expose probability, with values near zero representing a confident no. Innflow currently determines Choice acceptance using the selected option probability, Boolean acceptance using distance toward yes or no, and Score acceptance using returned confidence. Do not equate the Choice acceptance threshold with TypeSafe’s confidence statistic. If any question misses its policy requirement, the result takes Needs review. ## Meaningful test cases Include a clearly technical request, a clearly billing request, an unrelated message that maps to other, a mixed-intent message, and an incomplete request. Empty or unresolved input should be fixed rather than treated as a low-confidence decision. Explain how a timeout, unavailable service, or disabled workspace differs from an ordinary Needs review result. ## Credential and access guidance Do not ask readers to paste API secrets into workflow text, screenshots, or prompts. TypeSafe credentials belong to the server-side integration. For a workspace without AI Decision access, direct readers to confirm availability with the Innflow team; do not instruct them to toggle deployment environment flags. ## Publication verification Before the article is queued or published, capture the real enabled-workspace UI and run the sample workflow end to end. Verify picker visibility, configuration labels, saved values, both branches, and the output paths used in screenshots. Repository inspection supports the implementation description but does not establish hosted availability. ## Frequently Asked Questions Where do I find AI Decision in Innflow? Do I need a TypeSafe OAuth connection? What does Boolean mean compared with Noul? How do I route Needs review? Can I use JEV alongside the Innflow Copilot? ## Drafting and CTA Target a 2,000–3,000-word HTML tutorial with dedicated configuration code blocks, clear labels for illustrative examples, and the exact Frequently Asked Questions H2. Close with a small triage workflow that first creates a reviewable task rather than sending or deleting anything automatically. ## Sources and implementation evidence - [TypeSafe introduction](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction) - [Question primitives](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives) - [Confidence and review](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence) Innflow implementation inspected: src/tool-configs/ai-decision/block.ts; src/features/ai-decision/contracts.ts; src/features/tools/components/ai-decision/executor.ts; src/config/node-registry.ts. Validate hosted behavior and public access before publication.
